questions.question: A global company with a large number of AWS accounts is seeking a way in which they can centrally manage billing and security policies across all accounts. Which AWS Service will assist them in meeting these goals?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations centrally manages multiple accounts, enabling consolidated billing and organization-wide security policies (Service Control Policies). Trusted Advisor advises, IAM groups manage users in one account, and Config tracks configuration.

questions.question: Which service provides object-level storage in AWS?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 provides object-level (object) storage. EBS and Instance Store are block storage, and EFS is file storage.

questions.question: A company is concerned that they are spending money on underutilized compute resources in AWS. Which AWS feature will help ensure that their applications are automatically adding/removing EC2 compute capacity to closely match the required demand?
questions.explanation: AWS Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes EC2 capacity to match demand, eliminating spend on idle resources. ELB distributes traffic, Budgets alerts on cost, and Cost Explorer analyzes spend.

questions.question: Which S3 storage class is best for data with unpredictable access patterns?
questions.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on usage, making it ideal for unpredictable or changing access patterns. The other classes assume a known access frequency.

questions.question: What is the AWS database service that allows you to upload data structured in key-value format?
questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB stores data in key-value (and document) format. Aurora, Redshift, and RDS are relational/analytics databases.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding Amazon EC2 On-demand instances?

options.text: You have to pay a start-up fee when launching a new instance for the first time.
The on-demand instances follow the AWS pay-as-you-go pricing model.
With on-demand instances, no longer-term commitments or upfront payments are needed.
When using on-demand Linux instances, you are charged per second based on an hourly rate.

questions.explanation: The incorrect statement is that you pay a start-up fee — On-Demand instances have no start-up fee or upfront commitment, follow pay-as-you-go pricing, and are billed per second (Linux) on an hourly rate.

questions.question: A company has moved to AWS recently. Which of the following AWS Services will help ensure that they have the proper security settings? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor checks for security best practices and misconfigurations, and Amazon Inspector performs automated security assessments of workloads. SNS, CloudWatch, and the Concierge team are not security-configuration tools.

questions.question: What is the AWS feature that provides an additional level of security above the default authentication mechanism of usernames and passwords?
questions.explanation: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) adds a second factor on top of username/password, significantly increasing account security. KMS manages keys and email verification is not an auth-strengthening AWS feature here.

questions.question: A company is introducing a new product to their customers, and is expecting a surge in traffic to their web application. As part of their Enterprise Support plan, which of the following provides the company with architectural and scaling guidance?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure Event Management (IEM), available with Enterprise Support, provides architectural and scaling guidance to prepare for high-traffic events. The Concierge handles billing, and the Health Dashboard reports status.

questions.question: You work as an on-premises MySQL DBA. The work of database configuration, backups, patching, and DR can be time-consuming and repetitive. Your company has decided to migrate to the AWS Cloud. Which of the following can help save time on database maintenance so you can focus on data architecture and performance?
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database that handles provisioning, patching, backups, and disaster recovery, freeing the DBA from routine maintenance. Redshift is a data warehouse, DynamoDB is NoSQL, and CloudWatch is monitoring.

questions.question: Which of the below is a best-practice when designing solutions on AWS?

options.text: Invest heavily in architecting your environment, as it is not easy to change your design later.
Use AWS reservations to reduce costs when testing your production environment.
Automate wherever possible to make architectural (© ) experimentation easier.
Provision a large compute capacity to handle any spikes in load

questions.explanation: A core AWS best practice is to automate wherever possible, which makes experimentation and recovery easier and more reliable. AWS designs are easy to change, you treat servers as disposable, and over-provisioning wastes money.

questions.question: According to the AWS Acceptable Use Policy, which of the following statements is true regarding penetration testing of EC2 instances?

options.text: Penetration testing is not allowed in AWS.
Penetration testing is performed automatically by AWS to determine vulnerabilities in your AWS infrastructure.
Penetration testing can be performed by the customer on their own instances without prior authorization from AWS.
The AWS customers are only allowed to perform penetration testing on services managed by AWS.

questions.explanation: AWS permits customers to run penetration testing on their own resources for a set of approved services without prior authorization. AWS does not run pen tests for you, and it is not prohibited.

questions.question: Which service is used to ensure that messages between software components are not lost if one or more components fail?
questions.explanation: Amazon SQS is a fully managed message queue that durably stores messages so they are not lost if a producing or consuming component fails. SES sends email, Direct Connect is connectivity, and Connect is a contact center.

questions.question: The principle “design for failure and nothing will fail” is very important when designing your AWS Cloud architecture. Which of the following would help adhere to this principle? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: 'Design for failure' is supported by deploying across multiple Availability Zones (B) and using Elastic Load Balancing (C) to route around failures. MFA and pen testing are security practices, and vertical scaling does not add fault tolerance.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that provides a virtual network dedicated to your AWS account?
questions.explanation: Amazon VPC provides a logically isolated virtual network dedicated to your AWS account. A VPN is an encrypted tunnel, subnets are subdivisions of a VPC, and Dedicated Hosts are physical servers.

questions.question: According to the AWS Shared responsibility model, which of the following are the responsibility of the customer? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Managing environmental events of AWS data centers.
Protecting the confidentiality of data in transit in Amazon S3.
Controlling physical access to AWS Regions.
Ensuring that the underlying EC2 host is configured properly.
Patching applications installed on Amazon EC2.

questions.explanation: Customers must protect the confidentiality of their data in transit (B) and patch applications they install on EC2 (E). AWS handles data-center environmental events, physical access, and the EC2 host configuration.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services can be used as a compute resource? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 (virtual servers) and AWS Lambda (serverless functions) are both compute services. VPC is networking, CloudWatch is monitoring, and S3 is storage.

questions.question: Your company is designing a new application that will store and retrieve photos and videos. Which of the following services should you recommend as the underlying storage mechanism?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 is the recommended store for large, unstructured objects like photos and videos, offering durability and virtually unlimited capacity. EBS attaches to one instance, SQS is a queue, and Instance Store is ephemeral.

questions.question: Which of the following is equivalent to a user name and password and is used to authenticate your programmatic access to AWS services and APIs?
questions.explanation: Access keys are the credential equivalent of a username/password for programmatic access to AWS services and APIs. Key pairs are for SSH/instance login, and MFA is a second factor.

questions.question: What does Amazon ElastiCache provide?

options.text: An Ehcache compatible in-memory data store.
An online software store that allows Customers to launch pre-configured software with just few clicks.
A domain name system in the cloud.

questions.explanation: Amazon ElastiCache provides in-memory caching that accelerates read-heavy and latency-sensitive applications. It is Redis/Memcached compatible (not Ehcache), is not a software store, and is not DNS.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that enables you to manage all of your AWS accounts from a single master account?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations lets you manage all of your AWS accounts centrally from a single management (master) account. WAF, Trusted Advisor, and Config do not manage accounts.

questions.question: Which of the following EC2 instance purchasing options supports the Bring Your Own License (BYOL) model for almost every BYOL scenario?
questions.explanation: Dedicated Hosts give you visibility into the physical server and its sockets/cores, supporting BYOL for nearly every per-socket or per-core licensing scenario. Dedicated Instances isolate hardware but expose less licensing detail.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the benefits of moving infrastructure from an on-premises data center to AWS?

options.text: Free support for all enterprise customers.
AWS holds responsibility for managing customer applications.

questions.explanation: Moving to AWS converts large upfront capital expenditure (CapEx) into pay-as-you-go operating expense, reducing CapEx. AWS does not give free support to all, manage your apps, or auto-protect all data.

questions.question: Which of the following are important design principles you should adopt when designing systems on AWS? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Always use Global Services in your architecture rather than Regional Services.
Always choose to pay as you go.

questions.explanation: Key AWS design principles include automating wherever possible (D) and removing single points of failure (E). You should prefer the right Regional vs. Global service per need, treat servers as disposable, and pay-as-you-go is a benefit but not a 'design' principle in this list's intent.

questions.question: Which AWS Service can be used to establish a dedicated, private network connection between AWS and your datacenter?
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, private network link between your data center and AWS. CloudFront is a CDN, Snowball moves data physically, and Route 53 is DNS.

questions.question: You are working on two projects that require completely different network configurations. Which AWS service or feature will allow you to isolate resources and network configurations?
questions.explanation: A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) lets you isolate resources and define completely separate network configurations per project. Internet gateways, security groups, and CloudFront do not provide full network isolation on their own.

questions.question: Which of the following services can help protect your web applications from SQL injection and other vulnerabilities in your application code?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) inspects HTTP(S) requests and blocks common exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Cognito handles identity, IAM handles AWS permissions, and Aurora is a database.

questions.question: An organization needs to analyze and process a large number of data sets. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation: Amazon EMR runs big-data frameworks (Hadoop, Spark) to analyze and process large datasets. MQ, SNS, and SQS are messaging services.

questions.question: Based on the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following are the sole responsibility of AWS? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS alone is responsible for creating/maintaining the hypervisor (C) and for physical hardware maintenance (E). Installing software, configuring ACLs, and monitoring application network performance are customer tasks.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that provides you the highest level of control over the underlying virtual infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 gives the highest level of control over the underlying virtual infrastructure (OS, networking, storage). Redshift, DynamoDB, and RDS are managed services that abstract the infrastructure away.

questions.question: What are the default security credentials that are required to access the AWS management console for an IAM user account?
questions.explanation: An IAM user signs in to the AWS Management Console with a username and password. MFA is optional, security tokens are temporary credentials, and access keys are for programmatic access.

questions.question: In your on-premises environment, you can create as many virtual servers as you need from a single template. What can you use to perform the same in AWS?
questions.explanation: An Amazon Machine Image (AMI) is a template you can use to launch as many identically configured EC2 instances as needed. IAM is permissions, an internet gateway is networking, and an EBS snapshot is a volume backup.

questions.question: What are two advantages of using Cloud Computing over using traditional data centers? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Cloud computing advantages over traditional data centers include eliminating single points of failure (B) through multi-AZ design and using globally distributed infrastructure (C). Reserved capacity and dedicated hosting are not inherent cloud advantages.

questions.question: Which of the following aspects of security are managed by AWS? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS manages hardware patching (D) and the security of the global physical infrastructure (E). EBS encryption, VPC security, and access permissions are customer responsibilities.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the operational excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.text: The ability of a system to recover gracefully from failure.
The efficient use of computing resources to meet requirements.
The ability to monitor systems and improve supporting processes and procedures.
The ability to manage datacenter operations more efficiently.

questions.explanation: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems and continuously improving processes and procedures. Recovering from failure is Reliability, and efficient resource use is Performance Efficiency/Cost.

questions.question: AWS has created a large number of Edge Locations as part of its Global Infrastructure. Which of the following is NOT a benefit of using Edge Locations?

options.text: Edge locations are used by CloudFront to cache the most recent responses.
Edge locations are used by CloudFront to improve your end users’ experience when uploading files.
Edge locations are used by CloudFront to distribute traffic across multiple instances to reduce latency.
Edge locations are used by CloudFront to distribute content to global users with low latency.

questions.explanation: The non-benefit is distributing traffic across multiple instances to reduce latency (C) — that is load balancing, not an Edge Location function. Edge Locations cache content, speed uploads, and deliver content to users with low latency.

questions.question: What are the change management tools that helps AWS customers audit and monitor all resource changes in their AWS environment? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records who made API calls and AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes over time; together they support auditing and change monitoring. Comprehend, Transit Gateway, and X-Ray serve other purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following services allows you to run containerized applications on a cluster of EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: Amazon ECS (Elastic Container Service) runs and orchestrates containerized applications on a cluster of EC2 instances. Data Pipeline, Cloud9, and the Personal Health Dashboard are unrelated to container orchestration.

questions.question: Which of the following services will help businesses ensure compliance in AWS?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs API activity, providing the audit trail needed to demonstrate compliance. CloudFront is a CDN, CloudWatch is monitoring, and CloudEndure is migration.

questions.question: Which of the following procedures will help reduce your Amazon S3 costs?

options.text: Use the Import/Export feature to move old files automatically to Amazon Glacier.
Use the right combination of storage classes based on different use cases.
Pick the right Availability Zone for your S3 bucket.
Move all the data stored in S3 standard to EBS.

questions.explanation: Choosing the right mix of S3 storage classes for each use case (e.g., moving cold data to Glacier) reduces S3 costs. Buckets are not tied to a single AZ, and moving everything to EBS is not cost-effective.

questions.question: What are the AWS services/features that can help you maintain a highly available and fault-tolerant architecture in AWS? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling (B) replaces failed instances and adjusts capacity, while an Elastic Load Balancer (C) routes traffic only to healthy targets; together they enable high availability and fault tolerance. Direct Connect, CloudFormation, and NACLs do not provide this directly.

questions.question: Which of the following activities may help reduce your AWS monthly costs?

options.text: Enabling Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling for all of your workloads.
Using the AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) to load balance the incoming HTTP requests.
Removing all of your Cost Allocation Tags.
Deploying your AWS resources across multiple Availability Zones.

questions.explanation: Enabling EC2 Auto Scaling matches capacity to demand and avoids paying for idle instances, lowering monthly cost. Removing cost-allocation tags hurts visibility, and the other options do not inherently cut cost.

questions.question: What is the AWS service/feature that takes advantage of Amazon CloudFront’s globally distributed edge locations to transfer files to S3 with higher upload speeds?
questions.explanation: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront's edge locations to speed up uploads to an S3 bucket over long distances. WAF is a firewall, and Snowball/Snowmobile are physical transfer devices.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS security features is associated with an EC2 instance and functions to filter incoming traffic requests?
questions.explanation: Security Groups act as a stateful virtual firewall attached to an EC2 instance, filtering inbound (and outbound) traffic. NACLs operate at the subnet level, X-Ray traces requests, and VPC Flow Logs record traffic metadata.

questions.question: Which AWS services can be used to improve the performance of a global application and reduce latency for its users? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator (B) routes traffic over the AWS backbone to improve performance, and Amazon CloudFront (E) caches content near users; both reduce latency for global applications. KMS, Direct Connect, and Glue are unrelated to global latency reduction here.

questions.question: Using Amazon RDS falls under the shared responsibility model. Which of the following are customer responsibilities? (Choose TWO)
questions.explanation: With Amazon RDS, customers are responsible for the database schema (A) and database settings/parameters (C). AWS handles installing the engine, patching, and backups.

questions.question: A company has a large amount of structured data stored in their on-premises data center. They are planning to migrate all the data to AWS, what is the most appropriate AWS database option?
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS is the appropriate managed service for migrating large amounts of structured (relational) data. DynamoDB is NoSQL, ElastiCache is a cache, and SNS is messaging.

questions.question: A company has created a solution that helps AWS customers improve their architectures on AWS. Which AWS program may support this company?
questions.explanation: A company that helps AWS customers improve their architectures is an AWS Partner Network (APN) Consulting Partner. Technology Partners provide software products, the TAM is an Enterprise support role, and Professional Services is AWS's own consulting arm.

questions.question: What is the AWS serverless service that allows you to run your applications without any administrative burden?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda is the serverless compute service that runs your code without provisioning or managing servers. Lightsail, RDS, and EC2 all require managing instances.

questions.question: Jessica is managing an e-commerce web application in AWS. The application is hosted on six EC2 instances. One day, three of the instances crashed; but none of her customers were affected. What has Jessica done correctly in this scenario?

options.text: She has properly built an elastic system.
She has properly built a fault tolerant system.
She has properly built an encrypted system.
She has properly built a scalable system.

questions.explanation: Because the application kept serving customers despite three of six instances failing, Jessica built a fault-tolerant system (it tolerates component failure with no impact). Elasticity is about scaling to demand, not surviving failures.
